text:
elaine: Heads-up — onboarding sample app hitting a weird stall on first-run during the initial bulk embedding job. Users see the UI hang and nothing streams for ~20–30s.
kevin: Seen that before? Any logs we can look at quickly?
elaine: Pasted the relevant tail from the sampleapp run:
```
[2026-03-23T15:10:42Z] INFO starting bulk import: 120 items
[2026-03-23T15:10:42Z] WARN request 0 -> 429 rate_limited
[2026-03-23T15:10:42Z] INFO token_bucket: tokens=0 refilling in 1200ms
[2026-03-23T15:10:42Z] INFO backoff retry 1 in 1000ms
[2026-03-23T15:10:43Z] INFO auth retry -> fetching new token
[2026-03-23T15:10:43Z] INFO queued requests: 18
[2026-03-23T15:10:55Z] INFO resumed, first success
```
kevin: This looks like the SDK token-bucket is starting empty on init, so a burst immediately after boot waits for refill. Combined with auth retries queuing requests, you get a visible stall.
natalie: Triage idea: pre-seed the token bucket on SDK init (optimistic tokens) or implement a short soft-start that allows a small immediate burst. Also jitter initial backoff to avoid synchronized retries from multiple clients.
raj: Minimal repro I ran: start sample app, trigger import of 20 pages concurrently. Default sdk maxConcurrency=8, windowing=auto, tokenBucket capacity=10 but initial tokens=0 -> observed ~28s stall before any success.
devex-bot: Created issue RED-DEVEX-1234: client-sdk: prefill token bucket and add jitter to initial backoff (severity: medium).
elaine: Quick patch I tested locally (JS pseudocode):
```js
// on client init
const initialFill = Math.min(config.tokenCapacity, config.initialFill || 3);
tokenBucket.tokens = initialFill;
// backoff helper
function jitteredDelay(base, attempt) {
  const jitter = Math.random() * Math.min(100, base);
  return Math.round(base * Math.pow(2, attempt) + jitter);
}
```
kevin: For the sample app specifically, we can also prewarm by issuing a cheap HEAD to /v1/models or a single tiny embed on startup to warm auth and kernels. That avoids user-facing stalls without changing global defaults.
natalie: Agreed. For onboarding UX let's default to optimisticPrefill=3 and sampleAppPrewarm=true. Keep production defaults conservative.
raj: :thumbsup: I'll open a PR to update the sampleapp config, the JS/Go SDK defaults for dev-mode, and add a short note in the quickstart about "If doing large imports, set concurrency and prefill appropriately".
elaine: Can we add a CI smoke test that runs the sample import in headless mode to catch regressions? Fail if time-to-first-successful-request > 60s.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: branch client/preseed-tokens -> staging at 2026-03-23T15:20Z (pipeline #4587).
kevin: Nice. Also let's record a metric for onboarding: time-to-first-successful-request and expose it in Console per-route so we can see regressions from the field.
elaine: Thanks everyone, will follow up on the PR review.
